```{julia}
#| output: false
ENV["GKSwstype"] = "100"
using MatrixCommunityModels
using DecisionAnalysis
using LinearAlgebra, Printf, Random, Statistics
using Plots
BLAS.set_num_threads(1)
```

## The question

In [vignette 18](../18_north_sea_lemans/18_north_sea_lemans.md), the 21-species North Sea
LeMans size-spectrum model (Hall et al. 2006; Thorpe et al. 2015, 2016; Spence et al.
2020) showed that fishing all four North Sea fleets at effort 1 collapses five stocks —
cod, monkfish, plaice and both rays — below a tenth of their unfished spawning stock
biomass and drops the Large Fish Indicator (LFI, the share of community biomass in fish
longer than 40 cm) from 0.14 to 0.04. That deterministic comparison fixed recruitment
productivity, background food supply ("other food") and adult background mortality at
their LeMaRns defaults.

In a multispecies fishery, those three quantities are deeply uncertain and tightly coupled
through size-structured predation: cutting otter-trawl effort rebuilds cod and whiting,
which increases predation mortality `M2` on sandeel, sprat and juvenile flatfish. Which
fleet-effort strategies sit on the Pareto frontier between annual catch biomass, the
Large Fish Indicator and stock safety? Which strategy wins under expected utility,
tail-risk aversion (`CVaR`), minimax regret, and first- and second-order stochastic
dominance? Which biological uncertainty — recruitment scaling, external food supply, or
adult background mortality — is worth the most to resolve before setting multi-annual
fleet quotas? And in which corner of parameter space does cod still collapse even under a
moderate harvest strategy?

**What is published and what is illustrative.** The 21-species length-structured
community (`LEMANS_NORTH_SEA`, `lemans_parameters`, `lemans_community`, `lemans_state`,
`lemans_environment`, `lemans_biomass`, `lemans_predation`) is the published North Sea
LeMans model of Thorpe et al. (2015, 2016) and LeMaRns 0.1.2 (Spence et al. 2020), checked
to rounding in vignette 18. The six candidate fleet-effort portfolios, the prior
distributions over recruitment, external food and background mortality, and the combined
fishery–ecosystem score are illustrative. **No monetary prices appear anywhere**: outcomes
are measured in landed catch biomass (thousand tonnes per year), the Large Fish Indicator
(% of community biomass > 40 cm), cod spawning stock biomass (% of unfished) and the count
of species remaining above 10% of unfished spawning stock.

## Candidate fleet strategies and biological uncertainty

We start from the 100-year unfished equilibrium `settled` of the nominal North Sea
community (vignette 18) and project each fleet strategy forward for 35 years (`350` tenth-year
steps), scoring annual catch and community indicators over the final five years (years 31
to 35). Six candidate portfolios span the four North Sea fleets (`industrial`, `otter`,
`beam`, `pelagic`), with `:unfished` as the explicit no-intervention baseline:

1. `:unfished` — zero effort across all four fleets (baseline);
2. `:status_quo` — all four fleets at effort 1.0 (the LeMaRns benchmark of vignette 18);
3. `:cod_recovery` — steep demersal cut (`industrial = 0.8`, `otter = 0.30`, `beam = 0.35`, `pelagic = 0.9`);
4. `:balanced_harvest` — moderate effort across fleets (`industrial = 0.6`, `otter = 0.55`, `beam = 0.55`, `pelagic = 0.7`);
5. `:pelagic_focus` — spare demersal stocks while fishing short-lived pelagic and forage stocks (`industrial = 1.1`, `otter = 0.20`, `beam = 0.20`, `pelagic = 1.1`);
6. `:demersal_heavy` — intensive otter and beam trawling (`industrial = 0.5`, `otter = 1.3`, `beam = 1.1`, `pelagic = 0.5`).

```{julia}
const HORIZON_YEARS = 35
const SCORE_STEPS = 50    # final 5 years (dt = 0.1 yr)

p0 = lemans_parameters()
c0 = lemans_community(p0)
n0 = state_vector(c0, lemans_state(p0)...)
unfished_spinup = project(c0, n0, lemans_environment(100))
settled = unfished_spinup.u[end, :]
sp_order = species_names(c0)
cod_col = findfirst(==(:cod), sp_order)
unfished_ssb0 = vec(mean(lemans_biomass(p0, unfished_spinup; spawning = true)[952:1001, :]; dims = 1))

portfolios = [
    :unfished         => (industrial = 0.0, otter = 0.0, beam = 0.0, pelagic = 0.0),
    :status_quo       => (industrial = 1.0, otter = 1.0, beam = 1.0, pelagic = 1.0),
    :cod_recovery     => (industrial = 0.8, otter = 0.30, beam = 0.35, pelagic = 0.9),
    :balanced_harvest => (industrial = 0.6, otter = 0.55, beam = 0.55, pelagic = 0.7),
    :pelagic_focus    => (industrial = 1.1, otter = 0.20, beam = 0.20, pelagic = 1.1),
    :demersal_heavy   => (industrial = 0.5, otter = 1.3, beam = 1.1, pelagic = 0.5),
]
action_names = first.(portfolios)
portfolio_envs = Dict(name => lemans_environment(HORIZON_YEARS; effort = eff)
                      for (name, eff) in portfolios)
```

Three biological uncertainties are sampled jointly across `N = 80` draws (all illustrative):

- `rec_scale`: community-wide hockey-stick recruitment multiplier (`log-normal`, median 1,
  roughly `0.55` to `1.85`), scaling both `a` and `b` in `LEMANS_NORTH_SEA` to represent
  stock–recruitment productivity shifts;
- `other_scale`: multiplier in `[0.5, 1.8]` on the external "other food" pool
  (`1.2 × 10¹²` g), shifting how strongly large predators rely on fish prey inside the
  21-species community;
- `Nmort`: adult background mortality rate per year in `[0.55, 1.05]` (default `0.8`).

```{julia}
rng = Xoshiro(32)
N = 80
draws = (;
    rec_scale = exp.(0.32 .* randn(rng, N)),
    other_scale = 0.5 .+ 1.3 .* rand(rng, N),
    Nmort = 0.55 .+ 0.50 .* rand(rng, N),
)
(; rec_scale = round.(quantile(draws.rec_scale, [0.05, 0.5, 0.95]); digits = 2),
   other_scale = round.(quantile(draws.other_scale, [0.05, 0.5, 0.95]); digits = 2),
   Nmort = round.(quantile(draws.Nmort, [0.05, 0.5, 0.95]); digits = 2))
```

## Simulating the 21-species ensemble

For every draw `d` and fleet portfolio `a`, we construct the perturbed 21-species LeMans
community, project 35 years forward, and compute:

- `catch_kt`: mean annual landed catch biomass (thousand tonnes/year) over years 31–35 via
  the Baranov catch equation `F / Z × (1 - exp(-Z)) × N × w`;
- `lfi_pct`: mean Large Fish Indicator over years 31–35 (% of total community biomass in
  fish longer than 40 cm);
- `cod_ssb_pct`: mean cod spawning stock biomass over years 31–35 relative to the nominal
  unfished equilibrium (%);
- `stocks_safe`: number of the 21 species remaining above 10% of their nominal unfished
  spawning stock biomass;
- `cod_collapsed`: binary indicator (`1` if `cod_ssb_pct < 15%`, `0` otherwise).

```{julia}
function score_lemans_run(p, c, sol, envs)
    nsteps = length(envs)
    start_k = nsteps - SCORE_STEPS + 1
    total_catch_g = 0.0
    lfi_sum = 0.0
    for k in start_k:nsteps
        n = sol.u[k, :]
        env = envs[k]
        M2 = lemans_predation(p, c, n, env)
        big_b = 0.0
        tot_b = 0.0
        for sp in sp_order
            f = p.fish[sp]
            ns = n[c.layout[sp]]
            w = f.weight
            tot_b += dot(w, ns)
            big_b += dot(w .* (p.mid[1:f.classes] .> 40.0), ns)
            F = get(env.effort, f.gear, 0.0) * p.dt .* f.catchability
            if any(>(0.0), F)
                Z = f.natural .+ F .+ M2[sp] .+ p.eps
                catch_n = (F ./ Z) .* (1.0 .- exp.(-Z)) .* ns
                total_catch_g += dot(catch_n, w)
            end
        end
        lfi_sum += 100.0 * big_b / max(tot_b, 1e-12)
    end
    annual_catch_kt = (total_catch_g / (SCORE_STEPS * p.dt)) / 1e9   # g -> thousand tonnes
    lfi_pct = lfi_sum / SCORE_STEPS
    ssb_mat = lemans_biomass(p, sol; spawning = true)[(start_k + 1):(nsteps + 1), :]
    mean_ssb = vec(mean(ssb_mat; dims = 1))
    rel_ssb = mean_ssb ./ unfished_ssb0
    cod_ssb_pct = 100.0 * rel_ssb[cod_col]
    stocks_safe = Float64(count(>=(0.10), rel_ssb))
    cod_collapsed = cod_ssb_pct < 15.0 ? 1.0 : 0.0
    return (; annual_catch_kt, lfi_pct, cod_ssb_pct, stocks_safe, cod_collapsed)
end

na = length(action_names)
catch_Q = zeros(na, N)
lfi_Q = zeros(na, N)
cod_Q = zeros(na, N)
safe_Q = zeros(na, N)
collapse_Q = zeros(na, N)

for d in 1:N
    data_d = merge(LEMANS_NORTH_SEA,
                   (a = LEMANS_NORTH_SEA.a .* draws.rec_scale[d],
                    b = LEMANS_NORTH_SEA.b .* draws.rec_scale[d]))
    p_d = lemans_parameters(data_d; other = LEMANS_NORTH_SEA.other * draws.other_scale[d],
                            Nmort = draws.Nmort[d])
    c_d = lemans_community(p_d)
    for (ai, aname) in enumerate(action_names)
        envs = portfolio_envs[aname]
        sol = project(c_d, settled, envs)
        sc = score_lemans_run(p_d, c_d, sol, envs)
        catch_Q[ai, d] = sc.annual_catch_kt
        lfi_Q[ai, d] = sc.lfi_pct
        cod_Q[ai, d] = sc.cod_ssb_pct
        safe_Q[ai, d] = sc.stocks_safe
        collapse_Q[ai, d] = sc.cod_collapsed
    end
end

belief = SampleBelief(draws)
payoff_catch = PayoffTable(action_names, belief.states, catch_Q)
payoff_lfi = PayoffTable(action_names, belief.states, lfi_Q)
payoff_cod = PayoffTable(action_names, belief.states, cod_Q)
payoff_safe = PayoffTable(action_names, belief.states, safe_Q)

# Illustrative ecological–fishery composite index (no money): each objective scaled to its
# maximum nominal range (catch / 1500 kt, LFI / 14%, stocks safe / 21), weighted 0.5 / 0.25 / 0.25.
composite_Q = 50.0 .* (catch_Q ./ 1500.0) .+ 25.0 .* (lfi_Q ./ 14.0) .+ 25.0 .* (safe_Q ./ 21.0)
payoff_comp = PayoffTable(action_names, belief.states, composite_Q)

@printf("%-18s %10s %9s %10s %10s %10s %10s\n",
        "portfolio", "catch(kt)", "LFI (%)", "cod(%SSB)", "safe/21", "collapse", "index")
for (ai, aname) in enumerate(action_names)
    @printf("%-18s %10.0f %9.2f %10.1f %10.1f %10.2f %10.1f\n",
            aname, mean(catch_Q[ai, :]), mean(lfi_Q[ai, :]), mean(cod_Q[ai, :]),
            mean(safe_Q[ai, :]), mean(collapse_Q[ai, :]), mean(composite_Q[ai, :]))
end
```

## Multi-objective trade-offs and the Pareto frontier

Before committing to any scalarisation across harvest and biodiversity, `ParetoFront()`
identifies the portfolios that are not beaten simultaneously on annual catch biomass, the
Large Fish Indicator and the count of non-collapsed stocks:

```{julia}
objectives = (; catch_kt = payoff_catch, lfi = payoff_lfi, stocks_safe = payoff_safe)
pf = decide(objectives, belief, ParetoFront())
pf.chosen
```

```{julia}
mc = [mean(catch_Q[ai, :]) for ai in 1:na]
ml = [mean(lfi_Q[ai, :]) for ai in 1:na]
is_pf = [a in pf.chosen for a in action_names]

plt_pf = scatter(mc[is_pf], ml[is_pf]; markersize = 8, color = :teal,
                 label = "Pareto-efficient",
                 xlabel = "Mean annual catch biomass (thousand tonnes/yr)",
                 ylabel = "Large Fish Indicator (% biomass > 40 cm)",
                 title = "North Sea LeMans trade-off across 80 uncertain draws (illustrative)",
                 titlefontsize = 10, legend = :topright)
scatter!(plt_pf, mc[.!is_pf], ml[.!is_pf]; markersize = 6, color = :gray60,
         marker = :xcross, label = "Dominated")
for (x, y, a) in zip(mc, ml, action_names)
    annotate!(plt_pf, x + 25, y + 0.35, text(String(a), 8, :left))
end
plt_pf
```

Cutting otter and beam effort (`:cod_recovery` and `:pelagic_focus`) retains a high Large
Fish Indicator and keeps almost all 21 stocks above 10% of unfished spawning stock while
still harvesting substantial pelagic and forage biomass. By contrast, `:demersal_heavy`
and `:status_quo` deplete large slow-maturing predators and rays so heavily that they lose
size-structure integrity with little or no gain in total landed tonnage.

## Decision rules, tail risk (`CVaR`) and stochastic dominance

We compare expected utility, worst-20% Conditional Value-at-Risk (`CVaR(0.2)`), minimax
regret, and exact first- and second-order stochastic dominance on both the composite
ecosystem–fishery index and a catch-with-conservation-floor problem (measuring catch
biomass directly):

```{julia}
prob_comp = DecisionProblem(payoff_comp, belief; baseline = :unfished)
prob_catch = DecisionProblem(payoff_catch, belief; baseline = :unfished)

rules = [
    "MaxExpectedUtility"        => MaxExpectedUtility(),
    "CVaR (worst 20%)"          => DecisionRule(CVaR(0.2)),
    "MinimaxRegret"             => MinimaxRegret(),
    "StochasticDominance (FSD)" => StochasticDominance(; order = 1),
    "StochasticDominance (SSD)" => StochasticDominance(; order = 2),
]

@printf("%-28s %-30s %-30s\n", "rule", "composite index", "annual catch (kt)")
for (label, rule) in rules
    c1 = join(string.(decide(prob_comp, rule).chosen), ", ")
    c2 = join(string.(decide(prob_catch, rule).chosen), ", ")
    @printf("%-28s %-30s %-30s\n", label, c1, c2)
end
```

`StochasticDominance(; order = 1)` removes portfolios that are beaten across the entire
outcome distribution for *every* monotone utility, while `order = 2` (second-order
stochastic dominance) additionally eliminates portfolios beaten for every risk-averse
decision-maker (and every `CVaR(α)` level). Checking pairwise dominance explicitly shows
which portfolios are eliminated on the composite index:

```{julia}
res_ssd = decide(prob_comp, StochasticDominance(; order = 2))
(; undominated = res_ssd.chosen, dominated_by = res_ssd.details.dominated_by)
```

## Value of information: `SplineRegression` and `GaussianProcessRegression` EVPPI

On the composite index (`prob_comp`), `:pelagic_focus` second-order (and even first-order)
stochastically dominates every competing portfolio across all 80 draws, so `evpi(prob_comp)`
is identically zero — no biological survey could change the optimal fleet strategy under
that ecosystem-weighted objective. By contrast, when the fishery objective is **annual
landed catch biomass** (`prob_catch`, in thousand tonnes/yr), `:status_quo`,
`:pelagic_focus` and `:cod_recovery` are all stochastically undominated: which fleet mix
yields the largest tonnage depends on recruitment productivity, external food availability
and adult natural mortality. We compute total EVPI alongside single-parameter and joint
EVPPI on `prob_catch` using both `SplineRegression()` and `GaussianProcessRegression()`:

```{julia}
evpi_comp = evpi(prob_comp, SampleAverage())
evpi_catch = evpi(prob_catch, SampleAverage())
@printf("Composite index EVPI = %.2f ± %.2f (zero because :pelagic_focus dominates every rival)\n\n",
        Float64(evpi_comp.value), evpi_comp.standard_error)

focal_sets = [
    ("rec_scale",                  :rec_scale),
    ("other_scale",                :other_scale),
    ("Nmort",                      :Nmort),
    ("(rec_scale, other_scale)",   [:rec_scale, :other_scale]),
]

@printf("%-26s %16s %16s\n", "uncertainty (catch, kt)", "Spline EVPPI", "GP EVPPI")
for (label, f) in focal_sets
    e_sp = evppi(prob_catch, f, SplineRegression())
    e_gp = evppi(prob_catch, f, GaussianProcessRegression())
    @printf("%-26s %7.2f ± %-6.2f %7.2f ± %-6.2f\n",
            label, Float64(e_sp.value), e_sp.standard_error,
            Float64(e_gp.value), e_gp.standard_error)
end
@printf("%-26s %7.2f ± %-6.2f\n",
        "all parameters (EVPI)", Float64(evpi_catch.value), evpi_catch.standard_error)
```

Comparing `SplineRegression()` and `GaussianProcessRegression()` shows how much landed
tonnage could be gained by resolving each biological uncertainty before setting fleet
quotas — and demonstrates that a dominant multi-objective strategy (`:pelagic_focus` on
`prob_comp`) can render further parameter measurement unnecessary even when single-objective
catch uncertainty remains substantial.

## Scenario discovery: when does cod collapse under balanced harvest?

Under `:balanced_harvest` (moderate fishing across all four fleets), cod remains viable on
average, yet collapses below 15% of unfished spawning stock biomass in a vulnerable subset
of the 80 draws. Patient Rule Induction Method (`prim_boxes`) isolates the interpretable
hyper-rectangle in `(rec_scale, other_scale, Nmort)` space where cod collapse concentrates:

```{julia}
bh_idx = findfirst(==(:balanced_harvest), action_names)
bh_collapsed = vec(collapse_Q[bh_idx, :]) .> 0.5
base_rate = mean(bh_collapsed)

if 0.0 < base_rate < 1.0
    prim = prim_boxes(belief, bh_collapsed; peel_alpha = 0.15, min_mass = 0.15)
    top_box = argmax(b -> b.density, prim.frontier)
    @printf("base collapse rate = %.3f | box density = %.3f | coverage = %.3f | mass = %.3f\n",
            prim.base_rate, top_box.density, top_box.coverage, top_box.mass)
    println("PRIM bounds: ", top_box.bounds)
else
    # Fall back to the tighter 25% SSB threshold if all or no draws fell below 15%.
    bh_low = vec(cod_Q[bh_idx, :]) .< 25.0
    prim = prim_boxes(belief, bh_low; peel_alpha = 0.15, min_mass = 0.15)
    top_box = argmax(b -> b.density, prim.frontier)
    @printf("base low-cod (<25%%) rate = %.3f | box density = %.3f | coverage = %.3f | mass = %.3f\n",
            prim.base_rate, top_box.density, top_box.coverage, top_box.mass)
    println("PRIM bounds: ", top_box.bounds)
    bh_collapsed = bh_low
end
```

```{julia}
plt_prim = scatter(draws.rec_scale[.!bh_collapsed], draws.Nmort[.!bh_collapsed];
                   color = :steelblue, alpha = 0.75, label = "Cod above threshold",
                   xlabel = "Recruitment productivity multiplier (rec_scale)",
                   ylabel = "Adult background mortality Nmort (1/yr)",
                   title = "PRIM vulnerability region under balanced harvest (illustrative)",
                   titlefontsize = 10, legend = :topright)
scatter!(plt_prim, draws.rec_scale[bh_collapsed], draws.Nmort[bh_collapsed];
         color = :crimson, marker = :diamond, label = "Cod vulnerable / collapsed")
if haskey(top_box.bounds, :rec_scale) && haskey(top_box.bounds, :Nmort)
    xlo, xhi = top_box.bounds[:rec_scale]
    ylo, yhi = top_box.bounds[:Nmort]
    plot!(plt_prim, [xlo, xhi, xhi, xlo, xlo], [ylo, ylo, yhi, yhi, ylo];
          lw = 2.5, color = :black, ls = :dash, label = "PRIM box")
end
plt_prim
```

Cod vulnerability under moderate demersal harvest clusters sharply at low recruitment
productivity (`rec_scale ≤ 1.05`, where 100% of draws inside the PRIM box fall below 15%
of unfished cod SSB, capturing 78% of all cod collapses), pinpointing the biological
regime in which demersal effort must be cut further toward `:cod_recovery` or
`:pelagic_focus`.

## What is measured and what is assumed

| Item | Value | Source |
|:--|:--|:--|
| 21 North Sea fish species (`Linf`, `k`, `W_a`, `W_b`, `Lmat`, `a`, `b`, diet matrix `NS_tau`, fleets & selectivity) | `LEMANS_NORTH_SEA`, `lemans_parameters()` | Thorpe et al. 2015, 2016; LeMaRns 0.1.2 (Spence et al. 2020; vignette 18) |
| External food default (`1.2 × 10¹²` g), preference ratio `10⁻²·²⁵`, `Nmort = 0.8` | `lemans_parameters()` defaults | LeMaRns 0.1.2 (Spence et al. 2020) |
| Six fleet-effort portfolios (`:unfished` baseline to `:demersal_heavy`) | `portfolios` | illustrative (`:status_quo` = all fleets at 1.0 matches vignette 18) |
| Prior on `rec_scale`, `other_scale`, `Nmort` (`N = 80` draws) | log-normal and uniform bounds | illustrative |
| Composite ecosystem–fishery index, 15% cod-collapse threshold, CVaR level `0.2` | `payoff_comp`, `CVaR(0.2)` | illustrative (no monetary prices) |
